answer: In an agent marketplace serving harbor logistics and nebula mapping, every seller must lock a separate bond for 30 days before accepting jobs. A fake identity cannot reuse another identity’s collateral, so a swarm creates a ripple of capital demands: 1,000 identities with a $100 bond tie up $100,000. This does not prove identities are unique, but it makes multiplying them expensive through locked capital and its opportunity cost.
